clue.text: Fully 26 see cheap computer's content that anyone can read?

definitions.text: Fully 26 see cheap computer's content that anyone can read?

parts.words: Fully 26 see cheap computer's content that anyone can read?
parts.note: 26 is PEE, the name of the letter P, and see is the name of C; written out fully, the abbreviation PC is the full word for a card sent unsealed through the mail

explanation.surface: Someone notices what a bargain-basement computer is storing, and it turns out to be public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fully' asks for an abbreviation in full: 26 (PEE) and 'see' are the letter names P and C, and PC is short for the answer. 'cheap computer' tempts you to PC as personal computer; the message on the card is what anyone can read.
explanation.definitionFit: A message on an unsealed card sent through the post can be read by any postman or passer-by.

clue.text: First showing by PM before start of election

indicators.note: the prime minister's title comes ahead of the letter that follows

parts.note: PM stands for prime minister, also called the premier

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word election is taken

explanation.surface: A prime minister makes a first appearance just as the election campaign begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiere is the first public performance of a film or play.

clue.text: Lamb taco is served with cold dish of veal and ham

indicators.note: with here means accompanied by, the cold letter set in among the rearranged ones
food served up is dished out, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A lamb taco is brought out alongside a cold plate of veal and ham.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltimbocca is an Italian dish of veal escalopes topped with prosciutto and sage.

clue.text: To go viral badly, there's chance hot date's gone wrong

indicators.note: something gone wrong is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Why a video fails to go viral: an opportunity with an attractive date turned sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go viral' suggests internet fame, but means catching a virus.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch one's death is idiomatically to catch a very bad cold, a severe virus.

clue.text: One who gets up from chair is erotic

indicators.note: the letters are taken straight out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone rising from a seat finds the chair provocative.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gets out of bed, early or late, is an early or late riser.

clue.text: Culmination of a bit of play including own goal

indicators.note: the spelt-out letter name wraps around the abbreviation for own goal

parts.note: the first bit of the word play is P, written out as its letter name pee
OG is the standard football abbreviation for own goal

explanation.surface: A football match reaches its climax with a defender putting the ball into his own net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' takes the first letter of 'play' and writes it out as its letter name, as the cross-referenced 26 does; 'including' wraps that round the own-goal abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The apogee is the highest point of an orbit, so figuratively a peak or climax.

clue.text: Pretends not to be interested in obscure dramas?

definitions.text: Pretends not to be interested in

definitions.meaning: stage works that are difficult to come by, read literally

explanation.surface: Feigning boredom with arthouse theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays hard to get acts uninterested to make themselves more desirable.

clue.text: Cor anglais's third piece broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so the letter is written as it is said, its name
the third letter of the word anglais is picked out

explanation.surface: The third movement of a cor anglais concerto is put on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor anglais' is the woodwind instrument, but 'Cor' alone is the exclamation of surprise; the G of anglais is written as its spoken name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild British exclamations of surprise or admiration.

clue.text: Guarantee no right to come next

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: to guarantee something is to ensure it

explanation.surface: A promise that no right to take the next turn exists.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on afterwards, as a result or in time.

clue.text: Being governed by one's own in- law

parts.note: someone who is in is at home
a rule is a law or regulation

explanation.surface: Living under the authority of your own spouse's parents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in-law' reads as a relative by marriage, but splits into 'in' and 'law'.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-government of a region or country by its own people, especially as sought for Ireland.

clue.text: Stone age tools working the soil

indicators.note: working the soil churns it over, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Primitive farmers used flint implements to till the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Eoliths are crudely chipped flints once thought to be the earliest human-made implements.

clue.text: Asses working a long time need odd bits of rest

parts.note: a machine that is working is switched on
an age is a very long period

indicators.note: the first and third letters of the word rest are the odd-numbered ones taken

explanation.surface: Donkeys that have laboured for ages need a few scraps of relaxation.
explanation.definitionFit: Onagers are wild asses of Asia, so the plural names a kind of donkey.

clue.text: Area once under the British flag, taken by France in her broken English, say

parts.note: a flag is a kind of iris, the yellow flag being a wild iris

indicators.note: the letter for France sits within the jumbled word her
the word her is broken up and its letters rearranged

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
E is the abbreviation for English, followed by ..., which is what to say means

explanation.surface: A former British territory taken over by the French, described in her faltering English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like the British flag, but it is the plant iris; 'broken' rearranges HER into HRE and F goes in it to make HFRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish Free State (1922-37) was a dominion of the British Commonwealth before becoming Éire.

clue.text: See 12
Early article by magazine editor?

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
the editor heads Time, the American news magazine

explanation.surface: A piece produced before the deadline by a magazine's editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving before the scheduled hour means being early.

clue.text: Scot elected as PM, once

parts.note: Rab is a common Scottish familiar form of Robert
a party elected to power is in

explanation.surface: A Scotsman voted in as prime minister long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The PM is Israeli, not British.
explanation.definitionFit: Yitzhak Rabin was twice prime minister of Israel, assassinated in 1995.

clue.text: Relative has hard time getting drug after a month — admitted by 7 26?

indicators.note: the letters taken in are held between the two letters of the doctor's title

parts.note: 7 and 26 are GEE and PEE, the names of G and P, so together GP, a family doctor, abbreviated DR
Aug is the abbreviation for August
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A family member suffering a hard spell gets a drug a month later from the GP.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 and 26 are letter names that spell GP; a GP is a doctor, DR, and AUGHTE goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter is a female child, a close blood relation.

clue.text: Racing car taking 7 26, say, and Queen around Silverstone

indicators.note: the doctor's title and the queen's initials wrap around the two short abbreviations

parts.note: 7 and 26 are GEE and PEE, letter names giving GP, a family doctor, abbreviated DR
ER is Elizabeth Regina
silver is Ag, its chemical symbol, and stone is st, the British weight

explanation.surface: A racing car carries a GP and the Queen round the Silverstone circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Silverstone is the British Grand Prix track, and 'Grand Prix' hides in GP; here it splits into silver and stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragster is a car built for drag racing, short sprints on a straight track.

clue.text: See 6
Either half of two-thirds of nearly inactive substance

definitions.text: Either half of two-thirds of nearly inactive substance

parts.words: Either half of two-thirds of nearly inactive substance
parts.note: two-thirds of the word nearly is NEAR; each half, NE or AR, is the symbol of a noble gas, neon or argon

explanation.surface: A chemist halves a fraction of a nearly unreactive compound.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives examples rather than letters: NE (neon) or AR (argon), and 'inactive substance' then defines the class.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble gases such as neon and argon barely react chemically, so they are called inert.

clue.text: Sporting footwear with diamonds takes off

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

indicators.note: something gone off is spoiled, so the letters of takes are scrambled

explanation.surface: An athlete's shoe studded with jewels is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A boot with a blade for gliding on a rink is footwear worn for a winter sport.

clue.text: Russian composer loses address for US male sculptor

indicators.note: the composer's name drops a short word from its front

parts.note: Alexander Borodin wrote Prince Igor
Bo is American slang for a man, used as a form of address like buddy

explanation.surface: A Russian composer stops calling an American man by a nickname and becomes a sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker.

clue.text: Be a guarantor in respect of Wrong Trousers Day? FT? Not at first

definitions.text: Be a guarantor in respect of

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters are rearranged
only the opening letter of the word not is taken

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about backing a film called The Wrong Trousers, a day, and this newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wrong Trousers is a Wallace and Gromit film, but 'Wrong' is the anagram signal for TROUSERS DAY FT plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand surety for someone is to act as their guarantor, taking responsibility for their debt or bail.

clue.text: Little fish for Jack, the picky eater

definitions.meaning: Jack in the nursery rhyme who could eat no fat

explanation.surface: A small fish served to a fussy boy called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: In the English nursery rhyme, Jack Sprat could eat no fat and his wife could eat no lean.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small sea fish of the herring family; Jack Sprat is the rhyme's fussy eater.

clue.text: See 3
See 21
Religious leader raging briefly about bishop

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the letter for bishop
briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: rabid means furious or raging
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman furious for a moment about a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish teacher of the law and leader of a congregation.

clue.text: Make good theatre at city church

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
LA is Los Angeles
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Achieve success at a theatre in a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good a loss is to restore or substitute what was lost.

clue.text: Number one vegetable, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken sound, so the vegetable is given as it sounds

parts.note: a pea is a green vegetable

explanation.surface: The top vegetable, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' is a child's word for urinating, not first place.
explanation.definitionFit: In nursery slang a number one is urination, as against a number two.

clue.text: German repeatedly into living as mendicant

indicators.note: the doubled letter goes within the word for existing

parts.note: being, as in a living being, means existing or alive

indicators.note: the abbreviation is used twice over

explanation.surface: A German keeps scraping a living as a beggar.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, mendicant describes someone living by asking for alms.

clue.text: Develop the ability to chew 14, thanks initially to 18

parts.note: 14 reads as a head of Time, its first letter T, written out as its letter name tee

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word thanks is used

parts.note: 18 is a gas that does not react; helium is one, chemical symbol He

explanation.surface: A baby starts chewing, thanks at first to its gums.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references are read cryptically: 14, AHEAD OF TIME, gives 'a head of Time', T spelt TEE; 18, INERT GAS, gives an example, HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies teethe as their first teeth come through, letting them chew.

clue.text: Sluggish as shopper that's no jogger?

definitions.meaning: a shopper without a list, the memory jogger

explanation.surface: A slow shopper who is not out running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jogger' looks like a runner, but it is a memory jogger, a shopping list.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lethargic and lacking energy or enthusiasm is to be without spirit, the usual sense.
